high.title: Perry Warjiyo Resigns as Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: Perry Warjiyo has officially resigned as Governor of Bank Indonesia, with President Prabowo having received his resignation letter. Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti will serve as Acting Governor in the interim, as mandated by the BI Law. This is a significant market-moving event as leadership transitions at the central bank introduce uncertainty around monetary policy direction, interest rate decisions, and Rupiah stability.

high.title: Perry Warjiyo Resigns as Bank Indonesia Governor – Reasons Explained
high.summary: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo has voluntarily resigned from his position effective July 25, 2026, citing personal reasons. Deputy Governor Senior Destry Damayanti has been appointed as Acting Governor in the interim. This is a major market-moving event as leadership transitions at the central bank can significantly impact monetary policy direction, investor confidence, and Rupiah stability.

high.title: Destry Damayanti Appointed as Acting Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti has been officially appointed as Acting Governor of Bank Indonesia following Perry Warjiyo's resignation, as mandated by the Bank Indonesia Law. The appointment was announced by the Minister-Secretary of State Prasetyo Hadi at a press conference at BI headquarters. Markets will closely watch whether monetary policy continuity is maintained during this transition period.

high.title: Selection Process for New Bank Indonesia Governor Following Perry Warjiyo's Resignation
high.summary: Following Perry Warjiyo's resignation, the process for selecting a new Bank Indonesia Governor is now governed by the amended P2SK Law (UU No. 4 of 2026), which stipulates that the President will appoint a new governor in accordance with prevailing regulations. Destry Damayanti will serve as interim governor until a permanent replacement is confirmed. Investors should monitor the selection process closely as the new governor's policy stance will have significant implications for interest rates, Rupiah stability, and overall financial market conditions.

high.title: Business Community Urges Perry Warjiyo's Successor to Stabilize the Rupiah
high.summary: The Indonesian Employers' Association (Apindo) has called for a smooth leadership transition at Bank Indonesia, emphasizing that the new governor must prioritize Rupiah stability, inflation control, and financial system stability. Apindo Chairwoman Shinta Widjaja Kamdani warned that businesses are already grappling with global economic uncertainty, trade dynamics, exchange rate volatility, and high financing costs. A clear, credible, and predictable monetary policy communication during the transition is seen as essential to minimizing market volatility and sustaining investor confidence.

high.title: Perry Warjiyo Resigns as Bank Indonesia Governor
high.summary: Perry Warjiyo has officially resigned as Governor of Bank Indonesia, with President Prabowo receiving his resignation letter on Sunday, July 26, 2026. Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti will serve as Acting Governor in the interim, as stipulated by the Bank Indonesia Law. This is a major market-moving event as central bank leadership changes create significant uncertainty around monetary policy direction.

high.title: US Dollar Returns to Rp 18,000 Level Amid Perry Warjiyo's Resignation
high.summary: The US dollar strengthened against the Indonesian Rupiah by 130.4 basis points (0.73%) to Rp 18,038, breaching the psychologically significant Rp 18,000 level amid uncertainty following the BI Governor's resignation. Multiple sources including Bloomberg, Google Finance, and Investing.com all confirmed the Rupiah's weakening throughout the trading day. This represents a significant depreciation pressure on the Rupiah that investors and businesses with USD-denominated obligations should closely monitor.

high.title: Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) Closes Lower Following Perry Warjiyo's Resignation from Bank Indonesia
high.summary: Indonesia's benchmark stock index (IHSG) closed down 10.64 points (0.17%) at 6,185.77, pressured by the news of Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo's resignation. The index was volatile throughout the session, reaching a high of 6,219.41 and a low of 6,144.27, with 341 stocks declining versus 307 advancing. Trading volume was Rp 12.15 trillion, reflecting heightened market activity as investors repositioned amid the central bank leadership uncertainty.

high.title: Rupiah Under Pressure from US Dollar Following Perry Warjiyo's Resignation as BI Governor
high.summary: At market open on Monday morning, the US dollar rose to Rp 17,966, up 3 points (0.02%), directly linked to the announcement of Perry Warjiyo's resignation as Bank Indonesia Governor. Notably, the dollar weakened against other major currencies including the Australian dollar (-0.34%), euro (-0.38%), Singapore dollar (-0.13%), and Chinese yuan (-0.07%), suggesting the Rupiah's weakness is idiosyncratic and driven by domestic political/institutional risk. This signals that markets are pricing in uncertainty specifically related to Indonesia's central bank leadership transition.

high.title: Palace Guarantees Bank Indonesia Governor's Resignation Will Not Disrupt Economy
high.summary: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo has resigned and is temporarily replaced by Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti. The State Secretary Minister Prasetyo Hadi assured the public and business community that the transition will be transparent and will not disrupt monetary policy or national economic stability. This is a critical development for markets as central bank leadership changes can significantly impact monetary policy direction, interest rate expectations, and Rupiah stability.

high.title: Pegadaian Posts Net Profit of IDR 6.59 Trillion in H1 2026, Up 84.4%
high.summary: State-owned pawnbroker PT Pegadaian recorded a net profit of IDR 6.59 trillion in the first half of 2026, representing an 84.4% year-on-year growth from IDR 3.58 trillion in H1 2025. Total assets surged 53.9% to IDR 186.33 trillion, while gross outstanding loans grew 52.7% to IDR 155.1 trillion, driven by an adaptive business strategy and expansion of its gold ecosystem. Asset quality also improved, with the NPL ratio declining from 0.81% to 0.71%, signaling strong financial health for this key state-owned enterprise.

high.title: 490 Local Governments Struggling to Pay Employee Salaries to Receive Central Government Funding
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa has indicated the central government may inject additional funds into approximately 490 local governments struggling to pay employee salaries, including contract workers (PPPK), following cuts to regional transfer funds (TKD). This signals fiscal stress at the sub-national level and potential additional pressure on the central government budget. The final decision is pending presidential directive, making this a key fiscal policy development to watch.

high.title: Danantara Joins KSSK Meetings But Does Not Hold Policy-Making Authority
high.summary: Finance Minister Purbaya confirmed that Danantara's participation in Financial System Stability Committee (KSSK) meetings is limited to providing input and does not grant it voting or policy-making rights, clarifying that no revision to the Financial Sector Development and Strengthening Law (UU P2SK) is needed. This is significant for financial markets as it addresses concerns about the blurring of boundaries between the state investment fund and systemic financial oversight bodies. Investors and analysts will monitor whether Danantara's growing institutional presence could influence monetary and financial stability decisions.

high.title: Palace Guarantees Bank Indonesia Governor's Resignation Will Not Disrupt Economy
high.summary: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo has resigned and is temporarily replaced by Senior Deputy Governor Destry Damayanti. The State Secretary Minister Prasetyo Hadi announced the transition on Monday morning (27/7) at BI headquarters, assuring the public and business community that the process is transparent and will not disrupt monetary policy or national economic stability. This is a critical development for markets as central bank leadership changes can significantly impact monetary policy direction and investor confidence.

high.title: Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) Closes at 6,130, Down 0.89%
high.summary: The Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed down 55 points (0.89%) at 6,130 on Tuesday, July 28, 2026, opening already in the red at 6,175. The index hit a daily high of 6,199 and a low of 6,130, with total transaction value reaching Rp 10.85 trillion involving 25.43 billion shares traded 1,677,579 times. The decline likely reflects market nervousness following the abrupt resignation of Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo.

high.title: Indonesia Stock Exchange Urges Investors Not to Panic After Bank Indonesia Governor Resigns
high.summary: The Indonesia Stock Exchange (BEI) called on investors not to panic in response to the resignation of BI Governor Perry Warjiyo, describing it as part of broader economic, social, and political dynamics. BEI's Director of Trading Irvan Susandy acknowledged 2026 has been a particularly tough year for Indonesia, citing headwinds including Middle East war sentiment, MSCI index review warnings, and Moody's assessments. The exchange's public reassurance underscores the significance of the event and its potential impact on market sentiment.

high.title: Bank Mandiri Posts Rp 30.4 Trillion Net Profit in H1 2026, Up 24.4%
high.summary: Bank Mandiri (BMRI) reported a net profit of Rp 30.4 trillion for the first half of 2026, representing a 24.4% year-on-year increase driven by strong business growth. Third-party funds (DPK) grew 17.1%, loan assets expanded 19.9%, and net interest income (NII) rose 8%, while asset quality remained solid with an NPL ratio of 0.98% and cost of credit at 0.52%. This is a strong earnings result for one of Indonesia's largest state-owned banks and is likely to be a positive catalyst for BMRI shares.

medium.title: BGN Prepares Digital System for Parents to Monitor Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) Program Menus
medium.summary: The National Nutrition Agency (BGN) is developing a digital transparency platform allowing parents to monitor the Free Nutritious Meal (MBG) program by logging in with their child's national ID number (NIK) to view menus, kitchen facilities, and nutritional content. This initiative reflects the government's effort to strengthen governance and public trust in the flagship MBG program. Improved oversight mechanisms may influence the program's budget efficiency and supplier ecosystem, relevant to businesses in the food and catering sector.

medium.title: BGN Chief Bans MBG Kitchens from Using Subsidized Gas, Cooking Oil, and Rice
medium.summary: BGN Head Sudaryono has firmly prohibited MBG program kitchen units (SPPG) from using government-subsidized goods including 3kg LPG gas cylinders, Minyakita cooking oil, and SPHP rice, threatening sanctions and kitchen closures for violations. This policy aims to prevent misuse of subsidized goods and protect supply availability for lower-income households. The ruling has implications for commodity supply chains and the operational cost structure of MBG program suppliers.

medium.title: BGN Chief Threatens to Fire SPPG Heads Who Mark Up Food Prices in MBG Program
medium.summary: BGN Head Sudaryono has issued a stern warning against SPPG kitchen unit heads who inflate food procurement prices, classifying such acts as corruption and gratification violations punishable by dismissal and kitchen suspension. The agency is opening whistleblower channels for partners to report misconduct, signaling a tightening of governance over the large-scale MBG program. This crackdown is relevant to food suppliers and catering businesses participating in the government nutrition program.

medium.title: New Trend: Indonesians Now Using PayLater to Buy Groceries and Daily Necessities
medium.summary: A notable consumer behavior shift is emerging in Indonesia, with increasing numbers of people using Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) and digital credit services such as Kredivo to purchase daily necessities like groceries and mobile phone credit, rather than high-ticket electronics. This trend signals rising household financial stress and potential credit risk exposure in the consumer finance sector. For investors, it raises concerns about the quality of BNPL loan portfolios and the broader purchasing power of Indonesian consumers.

medium.title: 9 Civil Servant Employees at National Nutrition Agency (BGN) Facing Dismissal
medium.summary: The National Nutrition Agency (BGN) has dismissed 261 non-civil servant employees and is proceeding to terminate 9 civil servant (ASN) employees due to violations. BGN Chief Sudaryono announced the sanctions at a press conference in Jakarta, noting that those dismissed include 224 non-ASN staff and 37 expert advisors. This development may affect the operational efficiency of the BGN, which oversees the government's national nutrition and school meals program.

medium.title: PT Pos Indonesia Finally Settles Rp 24 Billion Sukuk Yield Payment
medium.summary: State-owned PT Pos Indonesia has completed the 6th periodic payment of its Sukuk Ijarah Berkelanjutan I Series A-C (2024 issuance), disbursing Rp 24.118 billion through Indonesia's central securities depository KSEI on July 24, 2026. The word 'finally' (akhirnya) in the headline suggests the payment may have been anticipated or slightly delayed, which sukuk holders and fixed-income investors should note. The successful settlement confirms the company is meeting its debt obligations to bondholders as per the trustee agreement.

medium.title: Village Cooperative (Kopdes Merah Putih) Managers' Salaries to Be Funded by State Budget for 2 Years
medium.summary: The Cooperative Ministry announced that managers of the Merah Putih Village/Urban Cooperatives (KDKMP) will have their salaries funded by the state budget (APBN) during the initial two-year operational period before transitioning to self-funded arrangements. The salary scheme will be regulated through a Presidential Regulation on KDKMP governance. This has implications for state budget expenditure and the long-term fiscal sustainability of the government's flagship cooperative program.

medium.title: Social Assistance to Be Distributed Through Kopdes Merah Putih, Pilot Program Set for August
medium.summary: The government plans to use Merah Putih Village Cooperatives (Kopdes Merah Putih) as a channel for social assistance (bansos) distribution, with a pilot program targeting 900 operational cooperatives expected to launch by end of August 2026. The initiative, confirmed by both the Cooperative Minister and Social Affairs Minister, represents a significant shift in the government's social welfare distribution infrastructure. This could impact the operational scale and financial flows managed by these cooperatives.

medium.title: Tomato Prices Plunge, Government Urges Regional Authorities to Launch 'Buy Local' Campaign
medium.summary: The National Food Agency (Bapanas) is responding to a sharp drop in tomato farm-gate prices from around IDR 12,000/kg to as low as IDR 1,000–1,600/kg due to oversupply, by organizing a 'buy local' campaign and selling tomatoes at IDR 6,500/kg to government employees. Bapanas is calling on regional governors, regents, and mayors to mobilize relevant agencies to support absorption of surplus harvests. This highlights ongoing food price volatility and the government's intervention mechanisms in the agricultural sector.

medium.title: Prabowo Aims to Eliminate Loan Sharks Through Village Cooperatives, Saving Hundreds of Trillions of Rupiah
medium.summary: President Prabowo Subianto stated that the Merah Putih Village Cooperatives (Kopdes) program is designed to eliminate predatory lending practices by loan sharks who charge farmers interest rates as high as 1% per day, replacing them with affordable financial services. This represents a major rural financial inclusion initiative that could reshape credit access for millions of Indonesian farmers. The program has broad implications for rural economic activity and the microfinance sector.

medium.title: Village Cooperative Managers' Salaries to Be Funded by State Budget for Two Years
medium.summary: Cooperative Minister Ferry Juliantono announced that the salaries of managers at Merah Putih Village Cooperatives (KDKMP) will be covered by the state budget (APBN) for the first two years of operations, after which cooperatives are expected to be self-sustaining. The arrangement will be formalized through a Presidential Regulation on cooperative governance. This adds to the fiscal commitments tied to the flagship Kopdes program, raising questions about long-term budgetary impact.

medium.title: Social Assistance to Be Distributed Through Merah Putih Village Cooperatives, Pilot Program in August
medium.summary: The government plans to pilot social assistance (bansos) distribution through 900 operational Merah Putih Village Cooperatives starting late August 2026, according to Cooperative Minister Ferry Juliantono and Social Affairs Minister Gus Ipul. This move would consolidate welfare distribution channels into the cooperative network, potentially improving efficiency but also expanding the operational and financial responsibilities of the Kopdes system. Investors in fintech, logistics, and rural banking sectors should monitor the rollout closely.

medium.title: BCA Records Rp 29.5 Trillion Net Profit, Loans Break Rp 1,000 Trillion Mark for First Time
medium.summary: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) reported a net profit of Rp 29.5 trillion in H1 2026, supported by 8% year-on-year loan growth that surpassed the Rp 1,000 trillion milestone for the first time, reaching Rp 1.036 trillion. The growth was underpinned by solid CASA (Current Account Savings Account) funding, which grew 10.2% year-on-year to Rp 1.082 trillion. This milestone reflects BCA's strong franchise and is a positive signal for BBCA shareholders and the broader banking sector.
